The inventor of the pie chart also had a plan to erase France from the map.

In 1793, William Playfair proposed carving up Revolutionary France among its enemies. Here's what it would have looked like — a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Playfair wasn't a general or diplomat. He was a Scottish engineer who basically invented modern data visualization — the line graph, bar chart, and pie chart all come from his 1786 and 1801 atlases.

2/ He'd also lived in Paris and watched the Bastille fall in 1789. By 1793, with the king executed and France at war with most of Europe, Playfair decided the Revolution itself was the threat — and dismemberment was the cure.

3/ His pamphlet: "Thoughts on the present state of French politics, and the necessity and policy of diminishing France." The title says it all — permanently shrink France so it could never threaten its neighbors again.

4/ The plan, mapped: Austria, Prussia and the Holy Roman Empire split the north. Spain annexes the southwest. Sardinia and the Papal States pick up scraps in the southeast. What's left is a small rump French state around Paris.

5/ It never happened — the First Coalition's armies couldn't even hold their gains, let alone execute a partition plan this ambitious. Napoleon would rise from the France Playfair wanted erased and conquer half of Europe instead.

6/ Playfair later worked against Revolutionary France in stranger ways too — including a scheme to counterfeit French currency to destabilize its economy from within.

Follow @forummapping for more forgotten maps like this.
